beats.narration: Before we turn anything, predict whether 3 rows of 4 squares will match 4 rows of 3.
Look across 3 rows of 4 squares, then predict what 4 rows of 3 will show.
Keep every square as the array turns from 3 rows of 4 into 4 rows of 3.
There are 12 squares in both views; turning the same squares changes rows, not the count.
The count stays 12 because rearranging the squares changes their grouping, not the squares themselves.
